restrictions: Two distinct 128-byte one-block messages m(a), m(b) of sha3-256-r24-prefix-v1 (zero state, rate 136, suffix 0x06 with pad10*1, rounds 0 to 23, full 256-bit digest). m(u) places the point u (lanes u0..u3) in lanes 1, 6, 11 = u0, u1, u0^u1^K11 and 4, 9, 14 = u2, u3, u2^u3^K14, the other lanes 0..15 fixed constants K (proof.md Section 2); m is injective. F(u) = digest of m(u) xor a fixed mask PD; F(a) = F(b) with a != b is an ordinary collision. Round 0 and round-1 theta are affine in u (a Guo-Liu-Song 2016 linear structure).

Distinguished-point parallel collision search (van Oorschot-Wiener) on F with 256 walks per step: DP = 114 top bits of F zero, cap Lc = 17 x 2^114 - 2 steps, at most 17,540 trails, a table of 5,847 words of three 85-bit records each (69-bit key of the end, used bit, 15-bit trail number; no length field; linear probing over words), the length of a matched trail rebuilt by replaying it to its first DP, Tb = 16967674 x 2^96 steps, a prefilter-hit counter that aborts the attempt at hit HMAX + 1 (HMAX = floor(Tb (1 + 2^-20)/2^8) + 1 + Lc), one replay with a looped one-walk program of F of 5,562 operations (proof.md Section 4).

Machine (declared heuristic H_machine): a register file of 1,024 words of 256 bits (1,018 for program values, 6 for the loop state), every load, store and register move is an instruction charged as one word operation, code counted at 32 bytes per instruction, no compact encoding and no interpreter. One step of 256 walks is 181,720 operations: sections AFF 3,084, GB 7,871 (run eleven times) and GA 8,298 (run eleven times), shared code, R23 701, with 33,206 loads, stores and moves of the allocation, plus loop 56, prefilter 17, counter 3 (Section 3).

Cost model collision-frontier-v5, unit 6504 (the organizer reference operation cost of sha3-256-r24, counted by its trusted counter): N = Tb x 181,720 + (3 x 5,562 + 37) x Lc + R + PRE = 250268067141319866828614231900210117585967 word operations, every loop-control, test, transfer and handler operation counted, the rebuild, advance and lock-step of the replay at most Lc evaluations each, at most HMAX + 1 prefilter hits at 207 each in every execution (Section 4); time_log2 = 124.85542 = log2(N/6504) rounded up, integer certificate 6504^100000 2^12485541 < N^100000 <= 6504^100000 2^12485542 (Appendix A).

Preprocessing, run by the attack and charged in N: the constant-selection run gen 512 (512 candidate constant sets, Appendix C), 513 x 2^32 + 512 x 2^10 operations, and the generator gen_s24ls (Appendix B), which selects the polarity pattern over all 2^25 patterns and the boundary size over 7 sizes and writes the program, 2^34 operations (measured 2^33.85 executed instructions); PRE = 2,220,498,616,320, preprocessing_log2 29. No advice.

Memory at most 1,048,576 bytes <= 2^20 (register file, program code at 32 bytes per instruction, other code with the looped replay F, spill cells, the table of 5,847 words, walk state; the search needs 1,028,576 bytes; Section 6). The two preprocessing programs run before the search: measured peaks (VmHWM, whole static image counted) 552,960 bytes for gen 512 and at most 1,028,096 bytes for gen_s24ls including the code region it writes; both also fit a 1 MiB sandbox that counts the declared span. memory_log2_bytes = 20, so normalizedTimeMemoryLog2 = 124.85542 + max(0, 20 - 20) = 124.85542; the Python experiments are reduced-width evidence, not the attack.

Success at least 0.39 for one attempt over the fresh word rho, under the score-critical premise H_rand, an assumption and not a proof: over the algorithm's coins (the random word rho), the program run on the fixed SHA3-256 target succeeds with probability at least the probability computed in proof.md Section 5 for a uniformly random function F, with failure terms for cut trails, the trail limit, self-coincidence, starts on trails, 69-bit key matches of different ends, further coincidences on the common path, and the hit-counter abort F5 < 2^-1000 proved by a Chernoff bound (Section 5). No full-scale run and no full collision is claimed.

heuristics.statement: Premise H_rand (an assumption, not proved): over the algorithm's coins, the program run on the fixed SHA3-256-r24 target (F(u) = SHA3-256-r24(m(u)) xor PD, with the linear-structure message embedding m of proof.md Section 2) succeeds with probability at least the probability computed in proof.md Section 5 for a uniformly random function F from 256-bit values to 256-bit values. The only coin of the algorithm is the uniform word rho; the target is fixed, and given rho the run is deterministic, so no hazard of 2^-256 per fresh evaluation is claimed for the fixed target. The computation of Section 5 is made in the random-function model, where F is realised by a lottery of independent uniform values, one per evaluation index (a fresh input returns its own value, a repeated input the stored one; a value is a distinguished point with probability 2^-114), whatever inputs the adaptive program chooses; there the first coincidence among e evaluations has probability at least 1 - exp(-e(e-1)/2^257), the length of the trail after it is derived from the flags of the lottery (Lemma 3), the exceptional histories (a trail repeating a point, a further coincidence on the common path, a start on a trail, a key match) are the failure terms F1 to F6 of Section 5, and one attempt succeeds with probability at least 0.39 after those terms. The premise is that the fixed target carries this probability over.
heuristics.scope: The fixed function F (the full 24-round permutation) of proof.md Section 2 on the points of one attempt: at most 1.011352 x 2^128 evaluations in 256 lockstep walks from starts rho + i, i < 17,540. Only the pair-coincidence rate among evaluated images and the distinguished-point rate enter the bound. The step program, the cost, the memory and the failure terms are derived, not assumed.
heuristics.extrapolation: Not an estimate of the success probability for the fixed target. Organizer-executed program checks: rho-w22 runs the whole search with the claimed program at width 22 (every trial returns a 22-bit partial collision the organizer recomputes, or nulls when the attempt halts at a failed replay or a budget, Section 4) and proj-w256 runs eight chained full-width steps and returns the first 22-bit agreement among the 2,048 iterates (a random function gives a success probability of 0.3934 per trial). Our own runs on the function F itself (proof.md Section 7.2, Appendix E): pair-coincidence rates on three windows among 2^24 images (32-bit windows) and 2^28 images (36-bit windows) of uniform inputs, of the consecutive starts rho + i and of chained iterates, and single-bit difference statistics.
heuristics.limitations: An assumption with no proof known to us. It is not tested at 256 bits: no run reaches 2^128 and no full collision is claimed. The checks work at 22 bits (organizer) and at 32 and 36 bits (our runs); they cannot show a deficit of a fraction of a percent or an effect that appears only for 256-bit coincidences. A pair-coincidence deficit eps costs about 0.5 log2(1/(1 - eps)) bits of time (0.0073 for eps = 0.01).

heuristics.statement: Machine convention: the 256-bit word RAM of collision-frontier-v5 with a declared register file of 1,024 words of 256 bits (1,018 hold program values, 6 the loop state), counted as memory (32,768 bytes). Every load, store and register-to-register move is an instruction and is charged as one word operation in every routine; no memory word is read or written except by a charged load or store. All code is counted at 32 bytes per instruction; there is no compact encoding, interpreter or decode convention (proof.md Section 3.2). The cost model and the target profile fix no register count and no code encoding.
heuristics.scope: The machine that runs the step program and the search of proof.md Section 4; it fixes the time and memory ledgers, not the success bound.
heuristics.extrapolation: None statistical: a declared convention. It is the convention of our blake3-r3 entry 0a9640ed (passed review) and of our sha3-256 entries aa2e6be6, 3183c941. Every transfer the program needs is written in the program (33,206 loads, stores and moves per step) and counted; the executed checks validate the function of this program, not the cost of register access, and the counts are those of the generated listing (Appendix B). The unit 6504 is the organizer reference operation cost of sha3-256-r24.
heuristics.limitations: A declared convention, not a measured property of hardware. The role supporting is the role of a declared convention and does not mean the choice is free: a smaller register file or another code encoding changes the time and memory ledgers and leaves the success argument unaffected.
